title: CUET Geography Test 12
subject: Geography / Geology (Code: 313)
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/Geography - 313.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: NTA CUET (UG) domain-paper format and public Geography shift analyses (no questions copied)
textbooks: NCERT Class 12 Fundamentals of Human Geography (rationalised)
NCERT Class 12 India: People and Economy (rationalised)
instructions: Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.
One set of 5 questions is based on a passage or table; the set stays together.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question: What is the long-staple (American) cotton grown in north-western India called?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Narma
Why: NCERT notes that India grows both short-staple (Indian) cotton and long-staple (American) cotton, called narma in the north-western parts of the country.
Why not the others: Desi (A) and kapas (C) are general words; boro (D) is a rice crop of West Bengal.
Key point: Cotton is a kharif crop.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about how the Census of India classifies workers:
(A) A main worker works for at least 183 days in a year.
(B) A marginal worker works for less than 183 days in a year.
(C) Marginal workers are counted as non-workers.
(D) Workers are grouped into cultivators, agricultural labourers, household industrial workers and other workers.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A), (B) and (D) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (C) is false — the Census has three groups: main workers, marginal workers and non-workers; marginal workers are workers. Every other option includes (C).
Key point: The work participation rate is higher in less developed areas.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question: Thorium is obtained mainly from monazite and ilmenite. Where are the world's richest monazite deposits found, according to NCERT?
options: A) The sand dunes of the Thar Desert
B) Beach sands of Palakkad and Kollam in Kerala
C) The old rocks of the Chota Nagpur plateau
D) The Ganga delta in West Bengal
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Beach sands of Palakkad and Kollam in Kerala
Why: NCERT notes that thorium is mainly obtained from monazite and ilmenite in the beach sands along the coasts of Kerala and Tamil Nadu; the world's richest monazite deposits occur in Palakkad and Kollam districts of Kerala.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not NCERT's monazite areas.
Key point: Thorium and uranium are used in nuclear power generation.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.sub_topic: The Cape of Good Hope route
questions.question: Which sea route, across the Atlantic Ocean, connects West European and West African countries with Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay?
options: D) The Cape of Good Hope route
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) The Cape of Good Hope route
Why: NCERT notes that the Cape of Good Hope sea route connects West European and West African countries with Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay; traffic on it is far less, because of limited development and population.
Why not the others: (A) links North America and Europe; (B) links North America with Asia; (C) passes through the Suez Canal.
Key point: South America and Africa have relatively little trade with each other.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: International Trade
questions.question: Maracaibo in Venezuela and Tripoli in Lebanon are examples of which type of port?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Oil ports
Why: NCERT gives Maracaibo, Esskhira and Tripoli as tanker oil ports; Abadan on the Persian Gulf is a refinery port.
Why not the others: Naval ports (B) include Kochi and Karwar; packet stations (C) include Dover and Calais; entrepot ports (D) include Singapore and Rotterdam.
Key point: Ports are classified by location and by the cargo or function they handle.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about outsourcing:
(A) It means giving work to an outside agency to improve efficiency and reduce costs.
(B) When it involves transferring work to overseas locations, it is called off-shoring.
(C) It is done only within one's own country.
(D) India, China, Eastern Europe, Israel, the Philippines and Costa Rica receive outsourced work.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A), (B) and (D) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (C) is false — outsourcing often involves transferring work overseas (off-shoring). Every other option includes (C).
Key point: Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) has grown with information technology.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Northern Atlantic sea route:
(A) It links north-eastern USA and Canada with north-western Europe.
(B) About one-fourth of the world's foreign trade moves on it.
(C) It links India with Australia.
(D) It is called the Big Trunk Route.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A), (B) and (D) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (C) is false — the route crosses the North Atlantic between North America and Europe. Every other option includes (C).
Key point: Both its coasts have highly advanced ports and harbour facilities.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question: India contributes about 21.6 per cent of the world's rice production. Where does it rank among rice producers?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Second, after China
Why: NCERT notes that India contributes about 21.6 per cent of world rice production and ranks second after China.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not India's rank.
Key point: Rice is the staple food of most people of India.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question:
Assertion (A): People who move out of a place are called emigrants.
Reason (R): People who move into a new place are called immigrants.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are NCERT's definitions and both are true. But they define two different groups of migrants, so the Reason does not explain the Assertion.
Why not the others: (A) treats one definition as the cause of the other; (C) and (D) need one statement to be false.
Key point: The place of origin loses population and the place of destination gains it.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: INSAT, established in 1983, is:
options: B) A helicopter service for remote areas
D) A satellite system for telecom and weather
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) A satellite system for telecom and weather
Why: NCERT notes that INSAT, established in 1983, is a multi-purpose satellite system for telecommunication, meteorological observation and various other data and programmes.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) are not satellite systems; a helicopter service (B) is Pawan Hans.
Key point: The IRS satellites are used for remote sensing.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: According to Census 2011, India's population accounts for about what share of the world's population?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 17.5 per cent
Why: NCERT notes that India's population of about 121 crore in 2011 accounted for about 17.5 per cent of the world's population.
Why not the others: About 2.4 per cent (A) is India's share of the world's area; (C) and (D) greatly overstate it.
Key point: India is the second most populous country after China (Census 2011).

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Planning and Sustainable Development
questions.question: Sustainable development takes care of which aspects of development, according to NCERT?
options: A) Only economic growth and incomes
B) Only the protection of forests and wildlife
D) Ecological, social and economic aspects
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Ecological, social and economic aspects
Why: NCERT notes that sustainable development takes care of the ecological, social and economic aspects of development.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) each take only one narrow part.
Key point: It meets present needs without compromising those of future generations.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The choices of some groups in India are limited by a lack of access to knowledge.
Reason (R): A large number of women and persons from socially and economically backward groups drop out of school.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both are true, and the Reason explains the Assertion — NCERT uses the dropping out of these groups from school to show how their choices get limited without access to knowledge.
Why not the others: (B) would need an unrelated Reason; (C) and (D) need one statement to be false.
Key point: Equity means equal access to opportunities for everybody.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.sub_topic: How land use changes with growth
questions.question: According to NCERT, which land-use category has increased as India's economy has grown?
options: A) Land put to non-agricultural uses
D) Permanent pastures and grazing land
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Land put to non-agricultural uses
Why: NCERT notes that land put to non-agricultural uses — buildings, roads, factories — has increased with economic growth and urbanisation.
Why not the others: Barren land (B), culturable waste-land (C) and pastures (D) have declined.
Key point: Area under forests has also increased, partly due to better demarcation.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
questions.question: According to NCERT, what is special about noise pollution?
options: A) It is spread evenly over the whole country
B) It is local, and weakens with distance from its source
C) It is caused only by natural events such as thunder
D) It travels through rivers to distant places
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) It is local, and weakens with distance from its source
Why: NCERT notes that noise pollution is location specific and its intensity declines with distance from the main source, such as industrial areas, arterial roads and airports.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are not true of noise pollution.
Key point: Noise is measured in decibels.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues and Problems
questions.question: How does NCERT describe the areas where slums develop?
options: A) As planned colonies on the best land
B) As exclusive areas with the best amenities
C) As areas reserved for government offices
D) As residential areas of least choice
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) As residential areas of least choice
Why: NCERT describes slums as residential areas of least choice, with dilapidated houses, poor hygiene and a lack of basic amenities.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) describe planned or privileged areas.
Key point: Most slum dwellers are rural migrants working in the unorganised sector.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: According to NCERT, what is meant by the density of population?
options: A) The total number of people in a country
B) The number of births per thousand people
C) The share of people living in cities
D) People per unit of land, usually per sq km
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) People per unit of land, usually per sq km
Why: NCERT defines density of population as the ratio between the number of people and the size of the land, usually measured in persons per sq km.
Why not the others: (A) is total population; (B) is the crude birth rate; (C) is the level of urbanisation.
Key point: Density = population ÷ area.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Planning and Sustainable Development
questions.sub_topic: Change in cropping in the canal area
questions.question: According to NCERT, how has the cropping pattern changed in the Indira Gandhi Canal command area?
options: A) Wheat and rice have been replaced by gram and bajra
B) Tea and coffee have replaced cotton
C) Wheat, cotton, groundnut and rice replaced gram and bajra
D) Farming has been given up for mining
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Wheat, cotton, groundnut and rice replaced gram and bajra
Why: NCERT notes that the traditional crops of the area — gram, bajra and guar — have been replaced by wheat, cotton, groundnut and rice.
Why not the others: (A) reverses the change; (B) and (D) did not happen.
Key point: Water-intensive crops have added to the problems of waterlogging and salinity.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Human Development Index, as described in NCERT:
(A) Health is assessed using life expectancy at birth.
(B) Education is assessed using the adult literacy rate and the gross enrolment ratio.
(C) Access to resources is measured in terms of purchasing power in US dollars.
(D) Each of the three dimensions is given a weightage of one-half.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT.
Why not the others: (D) is false — each of the three dimensions is given a weightage of one-third. Every other option includes (D).
Key point: The HDI score lies between 0 and 1.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: According to NCERT, how many people do areas with very heavy rainfall, or with extreme and harsh climates, generally have?
options: A) The highest densities in the world
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Low populations
Why: NCERT notes that areas with very heavy rainfall or extreme and harsh climates have low populations.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not supported by NCERT.
Key point: Mediterranean regions, with a pleasant climate, were inhabited from early periods.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question: Gatherers use different parts of plants. According to NCERT, which products are obtained from the bark of trees?
options: A) Quinine, tannin extract and cork
B) Rubber, balata, gums and resins
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Quinine, tannin extract and cork
Why: NCERT notes that bark is used for quinine, tannin extract and cork.
Why not the others: Rubber, balata, gums and resins (B) come from tree trunks; leaves give beverages, drugs and cosmetics (C); nuts give food and oils (D).
Key point: In modern times, some gathering has become market oriented.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: International Trade
questions.question: Which is the biggest port of India, with a spacious natural and well-sheltered harbour?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Mumbai
Why: NCERT describes Mumbai as the biggest port, with a spacious, natural and well-sheltered harbour.
Why not the others: Kandla (B) is a tidal port; Chennai (C) is an artificial harbour; Haldia (D) is a subsidiary of Kolkata.
Key point: Jawaharlal Nehru Port was built to relieve pressure on Mumbai.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Land Resources and Agriculture
questions.question: Which state accounts for more than half of the area under tea in India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Assam
Why: NCERT notes that Assam accounts for more than half of the cropped area under tea.
Why not the others: West Bengal (B, Darjeeling and Jalpaiguri), Tamil Nadu (C, the Nilgiri hills) and Kerala (A) also grow tea, but on smaller areas.
Key point: Tea is a plantation crop grown on hill slopes with heavy rainfall.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Development
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Idea)
(A) The Human Development Index
(B) Development as an increase in freedom
(C) Gross National Happiness
(D) The basic needs approach

List-II (Associated with)
(I) The International Labour Organisation
(II) Bhutan
(III) Amartya Sen
(IV) Mahbub-ul-Haq
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: Mahbub-ul-Haq created the HDI in 1990 (IV); Amartya Sen saw development as an increase in freedom (III); Bhutan uses Gross National Happiness (II); the ILO first proposed the basic needs approach (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Haq and Sen; (C) swaps Sen and Bhutan; (D) swaps Bhutan and the ILO.
Key point: These ideas all place people at the centre of development.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question: According to NCERT, what is cyberspace?
options: A) Electronic computerised space, encompassed by the Internet
B) The space above the atmosphere where satellites orbit
C) The area covered by a single mobile tower
D) The storage room of a computer
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Electronic computerised space, encompassed by the Internet
Why: NCERT describes cyberspace as the world of electronic computerised space, encompassed by the Internet such as the World Wide Web; it supports e-mail, e-commerce, e-learning and e-governance.
Why not the others: (B) is outer space; (C) and (D) are physical spaces, not cyberspace.
Key point: The Internet has widened communication across the world.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question:
Arrange the following forms of manufacturing from the simplest to the latest generation, as described in NCERT:
(A) Large-scale manufacturing
(B) Household (cottage) manufacturing
(C) High-tech industry
(D) Small-scale manufacturing
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: Household manufacturing (B) is the smallest unit; small-scale manufacturing (D) uses workshops and simple power-driven machines; large-scale manufacturing (A) uses assembly lines and large capital; NCERT calls high-tech industry (C) the latest generation of manufacturing.
Why not the others: (A) starts with small-scale units; (C) puts large-scale before small-scale; (D) puts high-tech before large-scale.
Key point: Each stage uses more capital, technology and specialised skills.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: The World Population
questions.question: In a year, a town recorded 5,000 births, 2,000 deaths, 1,500 in-migrants and 2,500 out-migrants. By how much did its population change?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) An increase of 2,000
Given: births = 5,000; deaths = 2,000; in-migrants = 1,500; out-migrants = 2,500.
Step 1: Natural growth = 5,000 − 2,000 = 3,000.
Step 2: Actual change = 3,000 + 1,500 − 2,500 = 2,000.
Common mistake: stopping at natural growth (3,000, option A), or adding out-migrants instead of subtracting them.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question: According to NCERT, the size of an industry depends on:
options: A) The age of its owner and the colour of its products
B) Only the area of land it occupies
C) Capital invested, number of workers and volume of output
D) Only the price of its products in the market
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Capital invested, number of workers and volume of output
Why: NCERT notes that the size of an industry depends on the amount of capital invested, the number of workers employed and the volume of production.
Why not the others: (A) is irrelevant; (B) and (D) each take only one, partial measure.
Key point: Industries are classified by size into household, small-scale and large-scale.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question: According to NCERT, where do most of India's metallic minerals occur?
options: A) In the alluvial plains of the Ganga
B) In the sand dunes of the Thar Desert
C) In old crystalline rocks of the peninsular plateau
D) In the young fold mountains of the Himalayas
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) In old crystalline rocks of the peninsular plateau
Why: NCERT notes that most metallic minerals occur in the peninsular plateau region in the old crystalline rocks.
Why not the others: Alluvial plains (A) and deserts (B) are poor in metallic minerals; the Himalayas (D) are young and less mineralised.
Key point: Over 97 per cent of coal reserves lie in the valleys of the Damodar, Son, Mahanadi and Godavari.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Geographer)
(A) Ratzel
(B) Ellen C. Semple
(C) Paul Vidal de la Blache
(D) Griffith Taylor

List-II (Idea)
(I) Neo-determinism, or "stop and go" determinism
(II) Conceptions from a more synthetic knowledge of the physical laws governing the earth and the living beings on it
(III) The changing relationship between the unresting man and the unstable earth
(IV) The synthetic study of the relationship between human societies and the earth's surface
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: Ratzel defined human geography as the synthetic study of the relationship between human societies and the earth's surface (IV); Semple as the changing relationship between the unresting man and the unstable earth (III); Vidal de la Blache spoke of conceptions from a more synthetic knowledge of physical laws (II); Griffith Taylor introduced neo-determinism (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Ratzel and Semple; (B) swaps Semple and Blache; (D) swaps Blache and Taylor.
Key point: All these definitions stress the relationship between humans and the earth.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question: India has about 14,500 km of navigable waterways. About how much do they contribute to the country's transportation, according to NCERT?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) About 1 per cent
Why: NCERT notes that India's navigable waterways contribute only about 1 per cent to its transportation.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) greatly overstate the role of waterways.
Key point: Waterways are cheap and fuel-efficient for bulky goods.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Human Settlements
questions.question: The Census of India classifies towns into six classes by population. A Class I town has a population of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 1,00,000 and above
Why: In the Census classification, Class I towns have a population of one lakh (1,00,000) and above; such towns are called cities.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are the population ranges of smaller classes of towns.
Key point: Cities with 10 lakh to 50 lakh people are million cities; those with more than 50 lakh are megacities.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: International Trade
questions.question: About what share of India's foreign trade by volume moves by sea, according to NCERT?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) About 95 per cent
Why: NCERT notes that about 95 per cent of India's trade by volume (and about 68 per cent by value) moves through ocean routes.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) understate the role of sea transport.
Key point: Ports are the gateways of international trade.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Gujjars, Bakarwals, Gaddis and Bhotiyas migrate from the plains to the mountain pastures in summer.
Reason (R): The mountain pastures stay covered with snow throughout the summer.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
Why: The Assertion is NCERT's example of transhumance. The Reason is false — these groups move up in summer because the high pastures are then free of snow, and return to the plains in winter.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) need a true Reason; (D) needs a false Assertion.
Key point: Transhumance is the seasonal movement of herders between plains and mountains.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Mineral and Energy Resources
questions.question: Which are the most important coalfields of the Damodar valley?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Jharia, Raniganj and Bokaro
Why: NCERT names Jharia, Raniganj and Bokaro as the most important coalfields of the Damodar valley.
Why not the others: (B) are oilfields of Assam; (C) are lignite areas; (D) are oilfields of Gujarat.
Key point: Jharia is the largest coalfield of India.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Human Settlements
questions.sub_topic: Industrial, religious, tourist and mining towns
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Type of town)
(A) Industrial town
(B) Religious and cultural town
(C) Tourist town
(D) Mining town

List-II (Example in NCERT)
(I) Singrauli
(II) Pachmarhi
(III) Tirupati
(IV) Bhilai
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT lists Bhilai among industrial towns (IV), Tirupati among religious and cultural towns (III), Pachmarhi among tourist towns (II) and Singrauli among mining towns (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps industrial and religious towns; (C) swaps religious and tourist towns; (D) swaps tourist and mining towns.
Key point: Towns are classified by their dominant function.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Tertiary and Quaternary Activities
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Node
(B) Link
(C) Time distance
(D) Cost distance

List-II (Meaning in NCERT)
(I) The expense of travelling on a route
(II) The time taken to travel on a particular route
(III) A road or route joining two nodes
(IV) The meeting point of two or more routes
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: a node is the meeting point of two or more routes (IV); a link is a road joining two nodes (III); time distance is the time taken on a route (II); cost distance is the expense of travelling on it (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps nodes and links; (B) swaps links and time distance; (C) swaps time and cost distance.
Key point: Every node joined by links forms a network.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: International Trade
questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Association of South-East Asian Nations (ASEAN)?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Jakarta
Why: NCERT's table of regional trade blocs gives Jakarta, Indonesia, as the headquarters of ASEAN.
Why not the others: Brussels (C) is the headquarters of the European Union; Vienna (D) of OPEC; Kathmandu (A) is linked with SAARC.
Key point: Regional trade blocs encourage trade between neighbouring countries.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the cultural environment created by human beings:
(A) Houses, villages and cities are part of it.
(B) Road and rail networks, industries, fields and ports are part of it.
(C) Mountains, rivers and natural vegetation are part of it.
(D) Items of daily use and other elements of material culture are part of it.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A), (B) and (D) follow NCERT's list of the elements of the cultural environment.
Why not the others: (C) is false — mountains, rivers and natural vegetation belong to the physical environment. Every other option includes (C).
Key point: Human geography studies the relationship between the physical and the cultural environment.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Transport and Communication
questions.question:
Arrange the following in the order in which they happened, from the earliest to the latest:
(A) The Border Roads Organisation is established
(B) The National Highways Authority of India becomes operational
(C) The Inland Waterways Authority of India is set up
(D) The Konkan Railway is completed
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (C), (B), (D)
Why: The BRO was established in 1960 (A); the IWAI was set up in 1986 (C); the NHAI became operational in 1995 (B); the Konkan Railway was completed in 1998 (D).
Why not the others: (B) puts the IWAI before the BRO; (C) puts the NHAI before the IWAI; (D) puts the Konkan Railway before the NHAI.
Key point: The BRO builds and maintains roads in border areas.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Secondary Activities
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Location factor)
(A) Access to markets
(B) Access to labour
(C) Government policy
(D) Agglomeration economies

List-II (Description in NCERT)
(I) Industries benefit from being near a leader industry and other industries
(II) Regional policies promote balanced development by setting up industries in particular areas
(III) Its importance has fallen as mechanisation, automation and flexibility have increased
(IV) Regions where people have high purchasing power attract industry
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT: markets with high purchasing power attract industry (IV); dependence on labour has fallen with mechanisation and automation (III); governments use regional policies for balanced development (II); agglomeration economies come from nearness to a leader industry and others (I).
Why not the others: (B) swaps markets and labour; (C) swaps labour and government policy; (D) swaps government policy and agglomeration.
Key point: Industries choose locations that maximise profit by reducing costs.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Population
questions.question: District X has an area of 2,000 sq km and a population of 10 lakh. District Y has an area of 3,000 sq km and a population of 5 lakh. What is the density of the two districts taken together?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 300 persons per sq km
Given: total population = 10 + 5 = 15 lakh; total area = 2,000 + 3,000 = 5,000 sq km.
Step 1: Combined density = total population ÷ total area.
Step 2: = 15,00,000 ÷ 5,000 = 300 persons per sq km.
Common mistake: averaging the two separate densities (500 and about 167 give about 333, option A).

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question: Why is commercial dairy farming described as labour intensive, according to NCERT?
options: A) Because it uses no machines of any kind
B) Because it is practised only on very small plots
C) Because animals are left to graze freely all year
D) Because of rigorous care in feeding and milking all year
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Because of rigorous care in feeding and milking all year
Why: NCERT notes that dairy farming is labour intensive, as it involves rigorous care in feeding and milking; there is no off-season during the year, as there is in crop raising.
Why not the others: (A) is false — dairy farming is also capital intensive, using milking machines; (B) and (C) do not describe commercial dairying.
Key point: Animal sheds, fodder storage and milking machines add to its cost.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Primary Activities
questions.question: Pastoral nomadism has three main regions. Which of these is its core region, according to NCERT?
options: A) The Amazon basin and the Congo basin of Africa
B) North Africa eastwards across Arabia to Mongolia
C) North-western Europe and eastern North America
D) The Pampas of Argentina and the Prairies
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) North Africa eastwards across Arabia to Mongolia
Why: NCERT describes the core region as stretching from the Atlantic shores of North Africa eastwards across the Arabian peninsula into Mongolia and Central China.
Why not the others: (A) are equatorial forests; (C) has mixed and dairy farming; (D) are grain-growing grasslands.
Key point: The tundra of Eurasia and south-west Africa with Madagascar are the other two regions.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport and Communication
questions.question:
The Orient Express runs from Paris to Istanbul. Arrange the following places on it from west to east:
(A) Vienna
(B) Belgrade
(C) Strasbourg
(D) Budapest
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C), (A), (D), (B)
Why: NCERT notes that the line runs from Paris to Istanbul via Strasbourg, Munich, Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade. So Strasbourg (C), Vienna (A), Budapest (D), Belgrade (B).
Why not the others: (A) puts Budapest before Vienna; (B) starts with Vienna; (D) puts Belgrade before Budapest.
Key point: The line shortened travel time between London and Istanbul by sea.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy: Water Resources
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Watershed management means the efficient management and conservation of surface water and groundwater. It involves preventing runoff, and storing and recharging groundwater through percolation tanks, recharge wells and similar methods. Haryali, a watershed development project sponsored by the Central Government, aims to enable the rural population to conserve water for drinking, irrigation, fisheries and afforestation; it is carried out by Gram Panchayats with people's participation. Neeru-Meeru (Water and You) in Andhra Pradesh and the Arvary Pani Sansad in Alwar, Rajasthan, have built percolation tanks, dug-out ponds (johads) and check dams through people's participation.

In Village V (illustrative), a house has a roof of 200 sq m, the area receives 600 mm of rain a year, and about 80 per cent of the rain falling on the roof can be collected.

Question: According to the passage, what does watershed management basically refer to?
options: A) Building large dams to generate hydro-electricity for cities
B) Efficient management and conservation of surface and groundwater
C) Diverting river water to cities for industrial use
D) Pumping more groundwater for irrigation
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Efficient management and conservation of surface and groundwater
Why: The passage, following NCERT, defines watershed management as the efficient management and conservation of surface and groundwater resources.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) are large engineering projects, not watershed management; (D) would deplete groundwater.
Key point: In a broad sense, it includes the conservation of all natural and human resources within a watershed.

questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Watershed management means the efficient management and conservation of surface water and groundwater. It involves preventing runoff, and storing and recharging groundwater through percolation tanks, recharge wells and similar methods. Haryali, a watershed development project sponsored by the Central Government, aims to enable the rural population to conserve water for drinking, irrigation, fisheries and afforestation; it is carried out by Gram Panchayats with people's participation. Neeru-Meeru (Water and You) in Andhra Pradesh and the Arvary Pani Sansad in Alwar, Rajasthan, have built percolation tanks, dug-out ponds (johads) and check dams through people's participation.

In Village V (illustrative), a house has a roof of 200 sq m, the area receives 600 mm of rain a year, and about 80 per cent of the rain falling on the roof can be collected.

Question: How much rainwater can the house in Village V collect from its roof in a year?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 96,000 litres
Given: roof area = 200 sq m; rainfall = 600 mm = 0.6 m; collection = 80 per cent.
Step 1: Rain on the roof = 200 × 0.6 = 120 cubic m.
Step 2: Collected = 80 per cent of 120 = 96 cubic m = 96,000 litres (1 cubic m = 1,000 litres).
Common mistake: forgetting the 80 per cent (1,20,000 litres, option A), or slipping a zero in the conversion (9,600, option D).

In Village V (illustrative), a house has a roof of 200 sq m, the area receives 600 mm of rain a year, and about 80 per cent of the rain falling on the roof can be collected.

Question: What do the three programmes described in the passage have in common?
options: A) They are all run by private companies for profit
B) They depend on local people taking part
C) They deal only with surface water, not groundwater
D) They all build very large dams in every village
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) They depend on local people taking part
Why: All three programmes in the passage depend on Gram Panchayats or local communities building johads, percolation tanks and check dams; NCERT stresses that people's participation is essential for watershed development.
Why not the others: (A) contradicts the passage; (C) ignores groundwater recharge; (D) — the structures named, such as johads and check dams, are small and local.
Key point: NCERT notes that there are only a few success stories, so awareness and participation need to be widened.
